From sign-in to getting started

Sign in as yourself

Make it work for you

Keep your everyday apps close

Star an app to add it to Your favourites. Search by name or description; on a keyboard, press / to search and Enter to open the first result. Favourites and recent-use hints stay in this browser; they do not sync to other devices.

Get useful notifications

Open the bell from any connected app. For Hub notifications, you can enable Slack direct messages in the notification panel if your organisation has connected Slack and your account can be matched. Some tools also have their own channels, such as Desk ticket threads.

Missing an app or a permission?

Your menu reflects the apps your organisation has made available to you. If Request access is shown, use it to explain what you need. Otherwise, contact your IT team. Access to an app does not automatically give you access to every record, teamspace or administrative setting inside it.

Manage your profile and sign-in

Open your profile at the top right to manage the options available to you, including your picture and sign-out. Company-managed profile information comes from your organisation’s directory. If a session expires, sign in again through the Hub; your work stays in the app.

Behind the scenes

What does a connected app receive?

The Hub shares your identity and the directory fields allowed for that app. Your administrator controls additional access, such as profile information, groups, roles and pictures. Each app controls access to its own records. Public features, such as the game leaderboard, have their own sharing rules.

How does the sign-in hand-off work?

For bundled apps, the Hub issues a single-use ticket valid for 90 seconds, bound to the intended app. That app redeems the ticket with the Hub and creates its own session. External software connected through OpenID Connect follows its configured sign-in flow; ordinary website links receive no Hub sign-in ticket.

What happens when access is removed?

Once the Hub records an account or access change, it sends a revocation update. Bundled apps also recheck their access data and deny access when it is 60 seconds old. Changes in an upstream HR or identity system take effect after they reach the Hub. External software has its own session policies.

What if the Hub is unavailable?

Opening connected apps requires the Hub. Bundled apps also stop accepting access when their authorisation data becomes too old. Try again once the connection returns; contact IT if the problem continues. A saved menu is a convenience, not a guarantee that an app is currently reachable.

Provider setup & attribute mapping
For your IT admin: Okta: SCIM app → Provisioning → connector base URL = the address above, unique identifier = userName, HTTP Header auth with the source's connection key (bearer token). Entra: Enterprise app → Provisioning → Tenant URL = the address, Secret Token = the key. Users and groups (Okta "Push Groups", Entra group provisioning). Two identity providers? Two sources, two keys — the same address can only be provisioned by one of them, and a group name must be unique across the hub. Attributes that arrive (title, department, division, organization, cost centre, employee number, manager, the work address as city/state/country, and any custom attribute your provider maps into its SCIM schema) show on the person card and can drive an app's exclude filters (Apps → the app → Who may use it → Advanced → Attribute filters, e.g. city^=Remote).
Add an Okta pull connection

Okta pull (advanced, optional)

Only if you cannot use the sync above: the hub reads your Okta directory itself every hour. Needs an Okta admin to set up an API integration.
Client-secret authentication (optional)
Okta setup (private_key_jwt, no SSWS tokens, no secrets): (1) Admin Console → Applications → Create App Integration → API Services → copy the client ID here and Add. (2) The hub then shows this connection's public key (JWK) — in the Okta app under General → Client Credentials switch to "Public key / Private key", Add key, paste the JWK, Save. Keep DPoP off. (3) Okta API Scopes tab → Grant okta.users.read — nothing else. (4) Admin roles tab → assign Read-only Administrator. Then Test.

Pull interval

How often the hub reads Okta. SCIM and event hooks update the Hub when received; suite apps enforce Hub changes within 60 seconds.
Lock-outs never wait for this interval: Okta event hooks apply them the moment Okta fires, and every app checks with the hub on each sign-in anyway.

Open Overview →
Operations: what needs attention across the stack?

Open Operations for current Desk, Trust, Assets, Contracts and Watch totals. Only apps where you have Admin access contribute. Each card shows its own scope and checked time. Failed or old checks stay visibly unverified; customer-project tickets stay separate from internal support. Continue in the source app to do the work. Owners can open Screens to pair a TV using selected aggregate sources and a fixed expiry. The TV uses a separate read-only key and never signs into your Owner account. Revoke it here when sharing should stop. Historical trends are planned separately.

Where should I make a change?

People: profiles, global Hub roles, groups and invitations. Permissions: roles in the six suite tools. Apps: connections, shared data and menu entries. Directory sync: people sources. Settings: company identity, sign-in and shared services.

What do employees see?

The employee workspace lists available apps. People can search, star favourites and open an app. The Apps button follows them between tools. The console is for Hub staff; an app login does not expose the console while it redirects.

One person, several ways to sign in

The Hub keeps a stable person ID. Email changes follow that person; reusing a departed person’s address must not transfer their access. A company account or an invited passkey connects the sign-in to that profile.

Company SSO or passkeys?

Company sign-in uses a configured provider such as Okta or Google. A passkey requires a linked profile, usually through a one-time invitation. People using company SSO do not also need a passkey. Configure company sign-in or view passkeys and invitations.

What happens when I open an app?

The Hub checks your session and app access, then issues a single-use ticket valid for 90 seconds. The destination app redeems it and creates its own session. During the handoff you see progress, with retry or return options if it fails. A direct app link preserves its destination through the sign-in. Ordinary website links use their own authentication.

Which groups can I edit here?

Manually created groups are edited in People. Active SCIM groups follow the identity provider. Manual groups that grant app roles can only be changed by a Hub owner. Assigning an IdP-managed group trusts that provider’s membership management.

How does directory sync affect Lunch?

Each SCIM source manages its own people and groups. Existing directory-only integrations such as Lunch retain their configured filters and sharing fields; they do not use the six-app permission model. Manage sources →

A colleague leaves. What should I do?

Deactivate the account in its source system, or lock it out in the Hub when immediate intervention is needed. Open Offboarding in Desk to plan or continue the case. Unexpected directory deactivations create an internal review there. Confirmed departures prepare hardware follow-up in Assets: plan returns, colleague handovers or sales, then confirm physical receipt and preparation. Desk reads the completion status automatically and checks it before closing. A former employee can use a private sale dealroom without restoring company access. Account reactivation pauses remaining work for review. Generic transfer remains available for other work; physical devices are handled in Assets. Retained app records do not become somebody else’s simply because an email address is reused.

Where are app roles managed?

For Assets, Contracts, Desk, Forms, Trust and Watch, Hub Permissions is the authority. Active global Hub owners and admins inherit Admin everywhere. App-specific assignments affect only that app. Endtools cannot add local administrators.

What does each role allow?

Employees see their own and explicitly shared or assigned records. App Admin includes all app content and settings, including personal Forms and Contracts areas. Desk Agent handles all tickets without app settings. Trust Fleet viewer reads the fleet. Watch Viewer reads all monitoring, so ordinary employees have no Watch access by default. Hub Helpdesk does not automatically grant an app role.

Can OpenTeam supply our people?

Yes. An owner can add it under Directory sync → OpenTeam, preview the import and enable a five-minute refresh. Existing emails are not automatically merged. Hub keeps login, app roles and Finance. Setup, safety checks and compatibility limits →

How do HR and Finance access on-call reporting?

In Permissions, select Desk and open Reporting access. Assign people or groups to existing on-call projects, choosing time review, compensation preparation, statement release or approved payroll export. Keep their base role as Requester to avoid support-agent access. No access still denies entry. Hub Owners/Admins inherit administration, but cannot approve their own service or release their own preparation. Open Service reporting in Desk for confirmation, review and CSV export. The hourly reporting alpha needs a reconciled company pilot before replacing an existing payroll spreadsheet.

Which assignment wins?

Inactive accounts have no access. For active people: global Owner/Admin → individual assignment → highest group role → app default. The effective role and its reason are visible before saving. Only Hub owners can delegate app roles; global Hub admins can inspect them.

When do permission changes take effect?

Apps refresh their directory every 30 seconds and refuse protected access when it is 60 seconds old. The bound starts after the Hub knows a change; upstream sync can add delay. “Confirmed by app” verifies the current snapshot and expires. Use Check app enforcement for a fresh observation; already downloaded data cannot be recalled.

Connect an app, external software or a website?

Connect an app offers three paths. Hub apps receive ticket sign-in and an allowed directory. External software uses OpenID Connect. A website is only a link and receives no Hub ticket. Menu visibility and access are separate choices.

Which data does an app receive?

Apps → the app → shared data controls optional profile, groups, avatars, notifications and service credentials. Identity and the central permission decision are essential to authorization. Turning off a profile field is not a way to revoke an app role.

What are Requests & reviews for?

They manage access-list apps and temporary group membership. They do not replace the central policies of the six tools. Previous reviews for centralized apps are historical records; use Permissions for their current roles.

Notifications, Slack and AI

Notifications contain a title and a link; content stays in its app. Slack delivery is optional and follows user preferences. Apps with AI access receive the configured provider credentials and send their own requests. Personal assistants use their owner’s app rights, not independent administrator rights.

How should I use backups?

Check protected services and schedules in Backups. Snapshots belong to individual services, not an atomic copy of the entire suite. Taking one can briefly pause that service. A restore replaces current data with the snapshot, so review the selected service and timestamp carefully.

How are apps installed and updated?

Use Apps → Add app to install a suite app or connect existing software. Under Apps → Updates, owners review published releases, see their notes and update the selected installation. Backend and frontend are snapshotted first; frontend files are published together and the completed release is verified. A failed step remains visible in History. Recovery is deliberate: restoring business data is never automatic.

Your operator publishes tested releases once using the release CLI. Hub and CLI use the same packages and update jobs. The package store is infrastructure; nobody needs to maintain a separate “Pantry” in their daily work. Direct deployments appear as current only when both parts match the published release. External integrations such as Lunch keep their own update process and directory sync. The update service itself is maintained by an operator.

New central-permission apps need a saved policy in Permissions before their first protected sign-in. Updating software never grants new data lanes or changes app roles.

Can I roll back a permissions update?

Restoring old app code also restores its old authorization rules and potentially retained local grants. Review matching Hub and app releases, data and access configuration together. A frontend-only rollback does not change backend access checks.

How do I recover access?

Keep a working Hub owner and a documented controller recovery path. Older principal-based grants appear under Settings → Hub administrators → Recovery access only if they exist. Link the holder to a person and verify the intended role before removing an old grant. Setup requires its one-time code or the actual controller; an unclaimed Hub is not open to its first visitor.

Who controls the infrastructure?

Application roles control normal app use. Infrastructure controllers can replace code or restore state and are outside that boundary. Your organisation chooses its Cloud Engine and operators; this alone does not guarantee confidentiality from infrastructure operators or a particular data location.

What happens if the Hub is unavailable?

New app sign-in needs the Hub. Existing protected sessions stop working once authorization data is 60 seconds old. A progress screen shows a failed handoff with retry and return options. External software follows its own session policies.

Where are sign-in and access changes recorded?

Activity records Hub events. Search by person, app or change. Stable identity, one-time app tickets and current backend permission checks remain the access boundary; hiding a control is not authorization.

Build a connected tool

Use the served SDK and onboarding guide. The backend redeems tickets, pulls the allowed directory and rejects stale authorization. The browser uses the shared sign-in and topbar components. Always enforce record access on the backend.

Compatibility and release discipline

Preserve stable state, compare signatures to committed baselines and exercise populated upgrades. Generate Candid and browser bindings from compiled code. Existing directory consumers keep their contract. Match frontend, backend, SDK copies and published recipes for a release.

Personal assistants

The kebab-mcp client connects with a person’s own Hub permission scope. See the assistant integration guide.

Architecture reference

Backups

Check protection, manage schedules and restore a snapshot. A restore replaces the service’s current data.

Backups are not switched on yet. Switching them on is a one-time IT task (terminal, about five minutes): send your IT person the Setup (IT) tab.
ServiceProtectedStateSnapshotsSchedule
Each app is one or two services running on your engine (technically: canisters). A snapshot pauses a service for a few seconds. Restoring puts it back exactly as it was — everything after that moment is gone, so the vault takes a safety snapshot first.

Schedules

The vault checks every 10 minutes. Daily runs happen in the hour you pick (UTC); interval runs when the last one is old enough. “Keep” rotates the oldest out (platform limit 10 per service).
ServicePlanKeepLast runResult

WhenWhoWhat
For the IT person. Three steps in a terminal, once. Afterwards owners run backups from the other tabs without touching a terminal again.

1 · Deploy the vault once

cd kebabstack/vault && mops install && icp deploy -e ic --subnet <SUBNET-ID> # then tell the vault which hub answers "is this person an owner?": icp canister call backend setHub '("")' -e ic

2 · Let the vault protect your services

Only a controller of a service may snapshot it. Run these with the identity that deployed each service (-f skips the confirmation prompt, which otherwise swallows the run); the vault becomes a co-controller — you keep yours. Then Re-check all on the Services tab.

Menu entries on custom domains, helper services, anything else on your engine. Its id from the Console or icp canister status.

Provider addresses

By default the hub is the identity provider under its own service address. With a custom domain, set both addresses here before the first app is connected — changing the issuer later means reconfiguring every app.

Company single sign-on (optional)

By default people sign in with the key on their device (passkey) — nothing to set up. If your company already signs in through Okta or Google, add it here and people get a "Sign in with Okta / Google" button on the menu. Setting this up is an IT task.

Add a sign-in provider
Setup instructions
Okta: Applications → Create App Integration → OIDC → Single-Page Application; Grant type Authorization Code (PKCE); Sign-in redirect URI = the URI above; assign the users/groups who may sign in. Google: Cloud Console → OAuth client (Web application) → same redirect URI. Who can actually log in is decided by the hub either way: only synced, ACTIVE users pass. Okta dashboard tile: set the Okta app’s Initiate login URI to <this hub>/?ssostart=<ID> (the ID column here).

Who runs this hub

Assign global roles in People. Owners manage permissions and recovery; admins manage day-to-day operations; helpdesk staff support sign-in and lock-outs. Global owners and admins inherit Admin in Assets, Contracts, Desk, Forms, Trust and Watch. Helpdesk app roles are assigned separately.
